messages:
maya: Morning team, excited to be here! Hitting a snag on local setup: using Colima + docker-compose, web service can't connect to Postgres. db service shows as Up in compose but my app logs "could not connect to server: No such file or directory" — seems like it's trying a unix socket.

taylor: welcome! that error often means your DATABASE_URL is missing host so the client falls back to unix socket. what does your env var look like?

maya: "DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@/devdb" — oops. changed to "postgres://postgres@localhost:5432/devdb" and now Postgres fails to start with "FATAL: could not create lock file './pgdata/postmaster.pid': Permission denied"

jake: yeah that's a mount permission problem — on Mac with Colima the host UID/GID mapping can make the data dir owned by root. either chown the host folder to the postgres UID (usually 999) or mount a named volume.

maya: tried `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata` and restarted, Postgres container comes up but my migrations error: "ERROR: could not access file \$libdir/pgvector" when creating extension pgvector

sam: pgvector isn't part of stock postgres image. you need an image with the extension preinstalled or build one. options: 1) use `ankane/pgvector:postgres15` image, 2) build Dockerfile FROM postgres:15 and `apt-get install -y postgresql-server-dev-all` + `make install` for pgvector in init, or 3) use an init container that runs `CREATE EXTENSION` after installing.

maya: switching to `image: ankane/pgvector:postgres15` fixed the pgvector error. to summarize for docs: - ensure DATABASE_URL includes host so client uses TCP - for colima on M1/arm, chown pgdata to 999:999 or use named volumes - use a pgvector-enabled image if your app requires that extension.

infra-bot: Note: added Colima + pgvector tips to dev-setup guide: https://go.redwood/dev-setup (:book:)

maya: thanks all! adding a short checklist to my onboarding notes and pinging @taylor to fold into the quickstart. :raised_hands:
